model_or_product: Schaller Fuzz / Kent 6400 / Blackfield / Höfner / Van Hall
flag_note: Effects Database explicitly groups Kent, Blackfield, Höfner and Van Hall with the Schaller Fuzz lineage. Track each retail identity separately while preserving one West German manufacturing lineage.

Kent 6406 The Angry Fuzz is a distinct larger fuzz-wah product associated with the Schaller family and shown at Musikmesse Frankfurt in 1971. Keep separate from compact Kent 6400 Distorter, but not as a separate builder.
Kent 6400 is documented as an OEM-branded version of the Schaller Fuzz. Model identity is separate from Kent 6406, while factory lineage remains linked to Schaller.

ToneHome and period advertising document Dharma Sound Sustainer in the 1970s and associate it with the Sola Sound/Colorsound ecosystem. Preserve Dharma Sound as a label, not an independent factory, until stronger evidence appears.
A 1977 Dharma Sound advertisement documents a small family of effects beyond the Sustainer. These should be cataloged as marketed products first, with manufacturing attribution left open.

model_or_product: Futuristic Sounds Sustain / Orange Sustain / Dharma Sound Sustainer
flag_note: ToneHome identifies the Futuristic Sounds Sustain as part of the same historical sustainer family as Orange Sustain and Dharma Sound Sustainer. Preserve the three labels separately until production documentation can establish exact manufacturer/customer roles.

Orange Sustain is documented as an English 1970s effect and appears in the same historical sustainer corridor as Dharma Sound and Futuristic Sounds. Do not count it as a separate manufacturer without stronger evidence.
Van Hall is listed among the marketed/OEM identities associated with the Schaller Fuzz family. Preserve the Van Hall label as a relationship node rather than creating a second West German factory.
